blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Full House Rewire Cost in Bristol? (2026 Guide)
blogPosts.excerpt: A comprehensive guide to understanding the costs, process, and timeline for rewiring a Bristol home, from terraces to detached properties.
body: Considering a full house rewire for your Bristol property? It's a significant investment but essential for safety, especially in older homes common in areas like Cotham, Redland, and Bishopston. The cost can vary widely, typically ranging from £4,000 to £8,000+ for an average 3-bedroom house. The final price depends on the property's size, the complexity of accessing old wiring, and the level of new sockets and switches you require.

Bristol's diverse housing stock means costs differ. A Victorian terrace with solid walls might be more labour-intensive to rewire than a modern property with cavity walls or conduit systems. Access is a key factor; chasing walls in solid stone buildings in areas like Clifton requires careful, professional work. We always recommend a detailed survey to provide an accurate, fixed quote for your specific home.

The rewire process typically takes 3-5 days for an average home. We isolate the electrical supply, safely remove the old wiring, install new circuits in compliance with BS 7671 regulations, and install your chosen accessories. We work to minimise disruption, often coordinating with plasterers for making good. A full rewire includes a new consumer unit (fuse box), which is the heart of your home's electrical safety.

A major benefit is future-proofing your Bristol home. A new rewire allows for additional circuits for modern demands like EV chargers, smart home tech, or high-power kitchen appliances. We can plan the installation to accommodate these needs from the start, avoiding costly additions later. This is particularly relevant for growing families or those planning home offices.

Crucially, a full rewire comes with an Electrical Installation Certificate (EIC), proving the work meets all safety standards. This is vital for insurance purposes and adds value to your property. At MPB Electrical, we handle all the certification and can advise on any notification required with Building Control under Part P.

To get an accurate cost for your Bristol home, we offer free on-site surveys. We'll assess your current installation, discuss your requirements, and provide a detailed, fixed-price quote with no obligations. This ensures you understand exactly what the work entails and what you're paying for before any commitment.

blogPosts.title: Emergency Electrician Bristol: What To Do When Your Power Goes Out
blogPosts.excerpt: Step-by-step advice for Bristol residents experiencing a power cut or electrical fault, including when to call an emergency electrician.
body: Losing power can be stressful, especially during Bristol's wetter months. Before calling an electrician, first check if it's a local area power cut. Use a mobile phone to check your utility provider's (Western Power or Bristol Energy) live power cut map online. If it's not a widespread outage, the issue is likely within your property.

Start with basic checks. See if neighbours are affected. Check your consumer unit (fuse box) – a switch may have tripped. Try resetting it by switching it to the off position, then firmly back on. If it trips immediately, there's a fault in your property's wiring or an appliance. Do not keep resetting it.

Identify the cause. Unplug all appliances in the affected circuit and try resetting the breaker again. If it holds, plug appliances back in one by one. If a specific appliance trips the breaker, it's faulty and needs replacing. If the breaker trips with nothing plugged in, you have a wiring fault – this requires professional attention.

Safety is paramount. If you smell burning, see scorch marks, or have sparking sockets, turn off the electricity at the main switch if it's safe to do so and call an emergency electrician immediately. Never attempt to investigate or fix suspected wiring faults yourself. Keep children and pets away from the affected area.

When to call MPB Electrical's emergency service in Bristol. If you've confirmed it's not an area outage, if your consumer unit is constantly tripping, if you have no power to essential circuits, or in case of any safety hazard (burning smell, sparking), call us immediately. We have electricians on call 24/7 across Bristol for rapid response.

We aim to be with you within the hour for genuine emergencies. Our Bristol-based electricians will diagnose the fault efficiently and carry out immediate repairs to restore power safely. We'll provide a clear explanation of the issue and a quote for any further work needed, ensuring your property is safe before we leave.

blogPosts.title: Bristol Landlord EICR Requirements: Your 2026 Legal Guide
blogPosts.excerpt: Everything Bristol landlords need to know about Electrical Installation Condition Reports, legal deadlines, and choosing a qualified inspector.
body: As a Bristol landlord, you are legally required to ensure the electrical installation in your rental property is safe. Since 2020, this means having a valid Electrical Installation Condition Report (EICR). For new tenancies, an EICR must be in place before the tenant moves in. For existing tenancies, you must provide a copy of a satisfactory EICR (no 'Code C1' or 'Code C2' observations) within 28 days of it being completed.

An EICR is not just a certificate; it's a detailed report on the condition of the property's fixed electrical wiring, sockets, lighting, and consumer unit. A qualified Bristol electrician will test the insulation resistance, earth continuity, and circuit functionality. The report will rate each circuit as satisfactory or unsatisfactory and note any observed damage or deterioration.

Choosing the right electrician is critical. The inspection must be carried out by a competent person – typically an electrician registered with a government-approved scheme like NICEIC, NAPIT, or ELECSA. MPB Electrical are NICEIC Approved Contractors, meaning our work is regularly assessed for quality and safety, and we carry the required insurance and qualifications to issue valid EICRs for Bristol landlords.

Cost is a common concern. For a standard Bristol rental property (e.g., a 2-bed flat in Bedminster), an EICR typically costs between £150 and £250. This is a small price for compliance and peace of mind. We provide a clear, fixed quote, and the inspection is usually completed within 2-3 hours with minimal disruption to tenants.

If the report identifies any 'C2' observations (danger present), remedial work is required. This could be something like replacing an old fuse box or faulty wiring. As your chosen Bristol electrician, we can provide a quote for any necessary repairs to bring the property up to standard, often carrying out the work quickly to avoid delays with tenancy agreements.

Keep your documentation organised. The EICR is valid for 5 years, but we recommend a visual inspection annually. You must provide a copy of the EICR to new tenants at the start of their tenancy and to existing tenants within 28 days of the inspection. Failure to provide a valid EICR can result in fines of up to £30,000 from Bristol City Council.

blogPosts.title: Why Upgrade to an LED Lighting Scheme in Your Bristol Home?
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover the benefits of switching to energy-efficient LED lighting in your Bristol property, from cost savings to enhanced ambiance.
body: Upgrading your Bristol home to an LED lighting scheme is one of the most impactful and cost-effective improvements you can make. Modern LED lights use up to 85% less energy than old incandescent or halogen bulbs and last up to 25 times longer. This translates directly into lower electricity bills – a significant saving given current energy prices in Bristol.

Beyond savings, LED lighting offers superior quality and flexibility. LEDs provide instant, full brightness without warm-up time, and they're available in a wide range of colour temperatures, from warm white (2700K) for living rooms to cool white (4000K) for kitchens and offices. This allows you to create the perfect ambiance in each room of your Bristol home.

For period properties in areas like Clifton or Cotham, LEDs are ideal. They come in styles that mimic traditional filament bulbs, preserving the character of a period room while delivering modern efficiency. We can also install dimmable LED systems, giving you complete control over lighting levels for different moods and occasions.

The environmental benefit is substantial. LED lights contain no hazardous materials like mercury and are 100% recyclable. By switching, you significantly reduce your carbon footprint. For Bristol residents committed to sustainability, this is a simple and effective step towards a greener home, aligning with the city's own environmental goals.

Professional installation ensures optimal performance. Our Bristol electricians can design a full LED scheme, calculating the right lumens (brightness) for each space. We handle the replacement of downlights, spotlights, and main lighting circuits, ensuring safe installation and compatibility with any existing dimmer switches or smart home systems.

To summarise, an LED upgrade is a smart investment for any Bristol homeowner. It lowers your energy bills, reduces maintenance costs thanks to long lifespan, improves light quality and control, and is better for the planet.
